'''''Dittrichia viscosa''''', also known as '''false yellowhead''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=DIVI6|taxon=Dittrichia viscosa|access-date=18 January 2016}}</ref> '''woody fleabane''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''sticky fleabane''' and '''yellow fleabane''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the [[Asteraceae|daisy family]].

''Dittrichia viscosa'' is a highly branching [[perennial]] common throughout the [[Mediterranean Basin]]. It has long, narrow leaves that are pointed at both ends and have teeth along the edges and [[Gland (botany)|glandular]] hairs on the surfaces. One plant can produce many yellow [[flower heads]] each with as many as 16 [[ray florets]] and 44 [[disc floret]]s.<ref>[http://www.maltawildplants.com/ASTR/Dittrichia_viscosa.php Malta Wild Plants, false yellowhead, ''Dittrichia viscosa''] includes photos, description, etymology, and other information</ref>

Originally, the species was found mainly in dry riverbeds and abandoned fields up to a 1500 m (5000 feet) elevation. Nowadays it is quite common in roadsides and [[ruderal]] habitats, even in urban areas. It is considered an [[invasive species]] in [[Australia]].<ref>[http://www.weeds.gov.au/publications/guidelines/alert/d-viscosa.html Weeds Australia, False yellowhead (Dittrichia viscosa) weed management guide] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090427024837/http://www.weeds.gov.au/publications/guidelines/alert/d-viscosa.html |date=2009-04-27 }} {{in lang|en}}</ref> The false yellowhead is a tough plant, very resistant to adverse conditions and [[degraded environment]]s. It is important as food for the caterpillars of certain butterflies and moths, like ''[[Iolana iolas]]''. The [[galls]] of the plants also are habitat for ''[[Myopites stylatus]]'' and ''[[Myopites inulaedyssentericae]]'', whose larvae are hosts to parasitic hymenoptera such as Eupelmus urozonus who are also major parasites of the [[olive fly]], helping control its population. This may be cause for its name in Catalan: ''Olivarda''.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.floracatalana.cat/flora/relacions-imatges?field_referencia_imatge_rel_value=VTax3046-Org124&field_tipus_de_relacio_target_id=&field_escala_rel_value=All | title=Relacions imatges | Flora Catalana }}</ref>

Despite the fresh-looking green color of its leaves and its attractive [[inflorescence]],<ref>[http://ichn.iec.cat/Bages/planes/Imatges%20grans/olivarda.htm Institució Catalana d'Història Natural, Flora del Bages - Olivarda] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091201051658/http://ichn.iec.cat/Bages/planes/Imatges%20grans/olivarda.htm |date=2009-12-01 }} in [[Catalan language|Catalan]] with photos</ref> this plant is sticky and has a certain smell that most people find unpleasant. It contains an [[essential oil]]<ref>[http://www.santllorenc.es/sessitges/itineraris/pdfs/herbesAromat.pdf  Ses Sitges, Sant Llorenç des Cardassar, Plantes aromàtiques] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107223758/http://www.santllorenc.es/sessitges/itineraris/pdfs/herbesAromat.pdf |date=January 7, 2010 }} in Italian, with photos and descriptions of several aromatic herbs</ref> and has been used in [[Complementary and alternative medicine|traditional medicine]] since ancient times, especially in the [[Levant]], as an [[astringent]].<ref>[http://www.inulav.com  /Inula_viscosa_Traditional_Medicine.html Avisco Ltd., Traditional medicine uses of ''Inula viscosa'']</ref>

In [[Elba Island]] and [[Corsica]] it is now used by residents and tourists to heal stings from [[jellyfish]], bees and wasps pressing fresh leaves on the skin with quick results.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} It is called in local dialect ''pescida''.

A yellow dye substance has, since ancient times, been produced from its roots.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ḳrispil|first=Nissim|author-link=|title=A Bag of Plants (The Useful Plants of Israel) |publisher=Cana Publishing House Ltd.|volume=3 (Ṭ.-M.) |year=1985|location=Jerusalem|pages=359–363|language=he|isbn=965-264-011-5 |oclc=959573975 }}, s.v. ''Inula viscosa''; syn. ''Dittrichia viscosa''</ref>

It is an important plant in [[Catalan tradition]], often mentioned in [[adage]]s and [[proverb]]s. One adage says that: ''"No vos 'nemoreu, amor, de cap fadrina gallarda que és com la flor d'olivarda molt guapa, i dolenta d'olor."''  [My dear one, don't fall in love with any woman who only has good looks, she is like a false yellowhead flower: beautiful, but full of stench.]
